GENERAL HEADQUARTERS
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIED POWERS
AG 710 (29 Nov 1945) PH
(SCAPIN-368)
29 November 1945
MEMORANDUM FOR : IMPERIAL JAPANESE GOVERNMENT.
THROUGH : Central Liaison Office, Tokyo.
SUBJECT : Prevention and Control of Typhus Fever in Japan.
1. In addition to the measures outlined in memorandum of 21 November 1945 for the Imperial Japanese Government, Subject: “Prevention and Control of Typhus Fever in Japan” (Reference: AG 710 (21 Nov 45) PH), it is desired that the responsible Japanese agency immediately institute further measures for the control of typhus fever as follows:
a. Disinfestaion by use of Insecticide, spray, DDT, residual effect at thirty (30) day intervals of the following:
(1) All railway cars assigned for use of Allied military personnel.
(2) All ferries operating between Aomori and Hakodate.
(3) Such other public conveyances that may be assigned for use of Allied military personnel,
b. After each disinfestation all conveyances will be plainly and uniformly marked as directed by the military command concerned to show date and place of treatment.
2. Military commands have been authorized to make Insecticide spray and equipment available as required for disinfestation.
3. Japanese civilian personnel will be provided by the Japanese agency concerned to carry out required disinfestation procedures.
4. United States military personnel will be available only for instruction and supervision of Japanese civilian personnel required to carry out the provisions of this memorandum.
FOR THE SUPREME COMMANDER:
H.W.ALLEN,
Colonel, A.G.D.,
Asst Adjutant General.
